## Final Project Structure

|              |                                          |
|--------------|------------------------------------------|
| **M1** · Now | **who** it is for what problem it solves |
| M2           | **how** it teaches                       |
| M3           | **how** it motivates                     |
| M4           | **who** it leaves out                    |
| Showcase     | the tool, and your defence of it         |

**AI will help create the tool.** *You* will decide who it is for, whether it is right, and whether it should exist.

## Activity {.divider}

## Be the AI Model **Groups by table. Ten minutes.**

| Pick a Sentence |                                               |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| A               | The cat sat on the \_\_\_\_.                  |
| B               | The student raised her \_\_\_\_.              |
| C               | During the exam, Maya passed Leo a \_\_\_\_.  |
| D               | The best way to learn algebra is to \_\_\_\_. |
| E               | AI and educational psychology could \_\_\_\_. |

1.  **Train** *(4 min)* — write five candidate words. Give each a probability. They must sum to 100.
2.  **Generate** *(3 min)* — draw a random number 1–100 on your phone. Pick the word in the list that is closest to the random number. That word is the output. **Do it three times.**
3.  **Discuss** *(3 min)* — what happened when a low-probability word came up?


## Prediction, not knowledge

An LLM predicts the **most likely next text**, given what it has read.

It has not met your learner. It has read a great many paragraphs *about learners like the one you described*, and it produces the most probable text about them.

**Fluent ≠ true.** **Confident ≠ verifiable sources.**

## What you could build in your final project

+-----------------------------------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------+
| Type                              | What it is                                                                                                           | Example                                                |
+===================================+======================================================================================================================+========================================================+
| **Chatbot tutor**                 | a chat with a written role, rules and a knowledge file — a *Socratic tutor* that asks before it tells                | a Custom GPT · a Gem · a Claude Project · a Poe bot    |
+-----------------------------------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------+
| **Teaching assistant**\            | the same chat, pointed at *your* work — practice sets, feedback, exit tickets, rubrics, differentiated versions      | a bot that turns one lesson into three reading levels\ |
| *(only with instructor approval)* |                                                                                                                      |                                                        |
+-----------------------------------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------+
| **Artifact**                      | a single interactive page the chat generates on request — a simulation, animation, a visualiser, a quiz, a card sort | *"make a quadratic I can drag"\                        |
|                                   |                                                                                                                      | *Practice for your unit                                |
+-----------------------------------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------+
| **Stand-alone page — static**     | an HTML file that lives on its own: Google Sites, GitHub Pages, a Canvas file. Same every visit.                     | **Tuesday's \                                          |
|                                   |                                                                                                                      | Week 4 instrument**                                    |
+-----------------------------------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------+
| **Stand-alone page — dynamic**    | a page that keeps state or talks to a model — a form that scores itself, an app with a login, a tutor with memory    | Forms + Sheets · Apps Script · Streamlit               |
+-----------------------------------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------+


## Code or no-code

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
**No-code**

-   a written role and rules *(system prompt)*
-   a knowledge file you upload
-   a form that scores itself
-   an artifact you asked for and kept

*You never see the code. The tool is the configuration.*
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Code**

-   you ask for the HTML, JavaScript or Python
-   you run it, and it breaks, and you ask again
-   you own the file — it works without the chat

*You never write the code. You read it, run it, and decide.*
:::
:::::

**Either way, the same two questions:** *who is it for, and what does it do that a handout cannot?*


## Prompts, tested {.divider}

## Vague vs. Contextualized {.smaller}

**Live.** Same tool, same question, twice.

AI output quality depends on the quality of the input: Can you trust the answer?

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Vague**

> *Explain quadratic equations to a student.*
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Contextualized** Developmentally appropriate

> *A 9th grader can execute the quadratic formula but cannot say what the answer is. They learn from diagrams and hands-on work before text. In under 120 words, describe what the two solutions* are *before any formula.*
:::
:::::


## Your turn — pick one {.smaller}

**Seven minutes, your own device, any chat tool.**

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Catch one**

Ask for something *real*, at a level of detail it cannot actually have:

> *What percentage of Mississippi 9th graders scored proficient on the Algebra I state test last year? Name the source.*

Then **open the source.** Is the number there?
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Build one**

> *Make a five-question quiz for \[your learners — can \_\_\_, cannot yet \_\_\_\]. Then tell me which question you are least sure fits them, and why.*

Read the answer to the second sentence first.
:::
:::::

**Critical Judgement:** How do you know the AI didn't hallucinate? Can you verify the output?

See this video from Dr. Casey Fiesler, an AI ethicist at the University of Colorado Boulder: <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0y7BSWoksyo>

## Austin's Five Questions {.smaller}

+---------------------------+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| Checkpoint                | The question you stop and ask                               |
+==========================:+=============================================================+
| **1 · Intent & Entry**    | *What am I asking for, and why this tool?*                  |
+---------------------------+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| **2 · Generate & Verify** | *Is this true? Where and how would I check?*                |
+---------------------------+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| **3 · Critique & Judge**  | *Does this fit my need (learners or the probable learner)?* |
+---------------------------+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| **4 · Refine & Decide**   | *What do I change, and what do I keep?*                     |
+---------------------------+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| **5 · Create or Resist**  | *Do I build this — or does a simpler handout do the job?*   |
+---------------------------+-------------------------------------------------------------+

At the centre: **your disciplinary judgement.** At every checkpoint: **× Resist** is an exit.

> **Reflection is the process.** Pause at each checkpoint. Question the output. Make a deliberate choice.
>
> You are responsible for the use and consequences of everything the AI gives you.


## Cognitive offloading

Handing a piece of thinking to something outside your head.

AI is most useful when it augments what you can do for your students

+--------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| **Offload the production**     | the HTML, the fifty practice items, the three reading levels, the first draft of the rubric |
+--------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| **Keep the judgement**         | who the learner is · whether the output is true · whether it fits · whether to build at all |
+--------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| **Be present for the learner** | if you've gained time, that's time for personal interaction and relationship building       |
+--------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

**You cannot use a tool well if you do not know what you asked it to do — or if you accept whatever it produces.**


## How to prompt using the checkpoints {.smaller}

+--------------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Checkpoint   | Habits to decide whether AI is appropriate or not                                                                                                        |
+=============:+==========================================================================================================================================================+
| **Intent**   | Write the ask in one line *before* opening the tab: *who · can/cannot yet · what output.* **If you cannot determine this, you are not ready to prompt.** |
+--------------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| **Generate** | Give it the learner, not the age. Ask for under N words. Ask it to name what it is least sure about.                                                     |
+--------------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| **Verify**   | How do you know it's true?\                                                                                                                              |
|              | One claim, checked by you, every time. Sources named; sources opened.                                                                                    |
+--------------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| **Critique** | *"Which of your assumptions about these learners could be wrong?"* — then decide if it is right.                                                         |
+--------------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| **Refine**   | Re-prompt with what it got wrong, not with "try again."                                                                                                  |
+--------------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| **Decide**   | Keep, change, or resist. Say which, and why, in your own words.                                                                                          |
+--------------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+


## Two versions of you

+----------------------------------------+-------------------------------------------------+
| **Competent and ethical user**         | **Not ready for AI**                            |
+----------------------------------------+-------------------------------------------------+
| Used AI as a tool                      | Outsourced the thinking                         |
+----------------------------------------+-------------------------------------------------+
| Struggled, failed, revised, improved   | Never sat with the confusion                    |
+----------------------------------------+-------------------------------------------------+
| Knows what good reasoning *feels* like | Guiding others through confusion they never had |
+----------------------------------------+-------------------------------------------------+

**The tool can do your homework. It cannot do your rehearsal — and if it did the homework, you likely didn't learn at all.**


## Exit card {.divider}

## Your prompt, twice

On the tool — **three minutes:**

**Before.** Write the prompt you would have written before this session.

**After.** The same request, contextualized to *your* learners — what they can do, cannot yet, how they learn — and one line asking the tool what it is least sure about.


## Milestone 1 {.smaller}

**One page. Five parts.** Instructions in Canvas, done in Packback.

1.  **Who** — *a class, a group, or one person; observed behaviours, not labels*
2.  **The problem** — *can \_\_\_ but cannot yet \_\_\_, because \_\_\_*
3.  **The tool type** — *and what it does that a handout cannot*
4.  **Assumptions blind spot** — *one default the AI would have about your learners, and how you can tell*
5.  **Synthesis** — *what Unit 1 predicts they will do with it*

Then **peer feedback** — critically challenge the work and provide suggestions.
